initial_reconstruction.claim: Summed EAL session time is longer than ordinary, with a substantial EAL context-construction component. Measured EAL sequence setup also exceeds ordinary but is shown on a much smaller separate scale. API-attempt transport/decode/accounting time dominates both session totals.
quantities: Top stacked bars show summed session time in seconds, partitioned into client API attempts, context construction and positive residual. Bottom horizontal marks show total measured sequence setup seconds on an explicitly separate 0-12 second scale; they are not additional context portions within the upper bars.

Upper stacked bars use gray for client API attempts, blue for context and orange for residual. Small residuals are visible only as thin right-edge orange slivers and ordinary context is too small to see, with exact values in caption. Lower setup marks also use blue, although the unqualified top legend labels that hue Context; the lower axis explicitly identifies setup.
initial_reconstruction.evidence_status: Observed instrumented timing components and a derived positive residual (session minus two recorded components). Sequence setup is measured separately. Operational boundaries cannot be interpreted as infrastructure costs.
initial_reconstruction.scope: All recorded donor and recipient sessions: 2,112 per arm, 4,224 combined. Components add once to each session-time sum and setup is added once separately if forming a whole run total. API attempt timing is a client boundary, not provider compute.
unintended_inferences: This descriptive timing partition supports locating recorded overhead in these operational components, and does not estimate provider internal compute, CPU time, infrastructure costs or end-to-end concurrent wall duration. Upper and lower lengths cannot be compared without accounting for their different scales.
